Care for every skin type

Skin health looks different on every skin tone.

Photodamage, pigmentation, and skin cancer risk present differently across the Fitzpatrick spectrum — skin types I through VI. Care here is built for your skin: assessed and treated for how it actually behaves.

The Skin Fitness method

Four phases. One year. Measurable skin health.

Skin Fitness is Rachel Cohen's framework. She created it and oversees it here, within Dr. Cohen's practice. Published in the Journal of Clinical and Aesthetic Dermatology (2026). You train your body over time; your skin adapts the same way. Each phase builds on the last, moving from a strong barrier to conditioned, resilient skin you can measure.

I Foundation

Barrier repair and baseline imaging. Every plan starts with a full medical skin exam.

II Active Training

Conditioning. Retinoids and actives are introduced gradually and titrated — dose follows tolerance.

III Performance

Once your skin is conditioned, targeted in-office work — peels, lasers, injectables — lands better and lasts longer.

IV Maintenance

Measure the outcome. Re-image, compare to baseline, and set the maintenance plan. Progress you can see.

It begins the way every relationship with this practice begins — with a comprehensive medical exam.

Baseline imaging
The program — now in pilot

A structured year of skin conditioning — Rachel's program, not a product counter.

Begin with a Skin Fitness assessment. From there, Rachel maps your skin's condition and builds a staged plan through the four phases — with objective measurement at checkpoints 1, 2, and 3 months. Especially valuable in perimenopause, when skin changes fastest.

The program is entering pilot: a first group of participants, measured closely. Public applications open beginning January 2027.

  • Plan built and reviewed with a clinician, every phase
  • Regimens titrated to your skin, not a product quota
  • Progress measured against your own baseline imaging
  • Phase check-ins in person or virtual — your choice
Book a Skin Fitness assessment with Rachel

Applying now joins the waitlist — places are held in order received, with first access when public applications open in January 2027.

About the practice

A medical practice, built for the long term.

Founded by Dr. Jay Cohen and grown deliberately, one credential at a time. Thirty years in the same community, at the same address.

Established in Needham

Dr. Cohen founded the practice and has provided medical dermatology to Needham and the surrounding communities for decades. He holds hospital staff appointments at St. Elizabeth's Medical Center and Newton-Wellesley Hospital, serves on the inpatient consultation service, and participates in the annual community-wide skin cancer screening.

Built deliberately

The practice added depth where it mattered. Dr. Kerry Fike brought double board certification in dermatology and micrographic dermatologic surgery. Rachel Cohen, NP-C, DCNP, brought two decades of patient care and a dermatology specialization. Marina Kitzis brought over thirty years of medical esthetics. Each addition answered a clinical need.

Thirty years in Needham

Dr. Cohen owns the practice and directs its clinical care. Three decades of patients from Needham and the towns around it, seen in one office on Hillside Avenue.

Meet our providers

Credentialed care. Every visit.

Three clinicians. Board certifications in dermatology, family practice, and Mohs-trained surgical expertise.

Jay L. Cohen, MD, JD

Dermatologist · Founder and owner

Dr. Cohen, a board-certified dermatologist, is a graduate of Cornell University and New Jersey Medical School. He completed his internship at Beth Israel Medical Center in New York and trained in dermatology at Columbia-Presbyterian Medical Center and the Boston University–Tufts joint program.

Before his residency, he engaged in research on nail growth and the treatment of fungal nail infections as part of a dermatopharmacology research fellowship at Columbia-Presbyterian — an interest he maintains, treating a wide variety of nail disorders. He holds hospital staff appointments at St. Elizabeth's Medical Center and Newton-Wellesley Hospital, where he is an active member of the inpatient consultation service and participates in the annual community-wide skin cancer screening. He is also a graduate of Boston University School of Law, admitted to the bar in New York and New Jersey.

  • Fellow, American Academy of Dermatology
  • Charter Member, Council on Nail Disorders
  • Massachusetts Academy of Dermatology · New England Dermatological Society
  • American Medical Association · Massachusetts Medical Society

Kerry Fike, MD, RPh

Dermatologist · Mohs surgeon

Dr. Fike is double board-certified in dermatology and micrographic dermatologic surgery. She is a graduate of Harvard Medical School and the Harvard Combined Dermatology Residency Training Program, with advanced Mohs surgery training at the Florida State University College of Medicine Micrographic Surgery & Dermatologic Oncology Fellowship at Dermatology Associates of Tallahassee.

She specializes in nonmelanoma skin cancer treatment, and also treats dysplastic nevi and other benign skin growths that may require dermatologic surgery.

  • Fellow, American Academy of Dermatology
  • Fellow, American Society for Dermatologic Surgery
  • Fellow, American College of Mohs Surgery

Rachel Cohen, NP-C, DCNP

Dermatology nurse practitioner · Creator of the Skin Fitness framework

Rachel, a dedicated family nurse practitioner, has nearly 20 years of experience caring for patients of all ages. In 2014 she pursued specialization in dermatology, achieving board certification through the Dermatology Nurse Practitioner Certification Board. She earned her BA from Boston University and her MSN from the MGH Institute of Health Professions.

Her practice is rooted in health promotion and disease prevention: helping patients attain optimal skin health through regular skin examinations and healthy skincare habits built into daily routines. She has a particular passion for non-surgical facial rejuvenation — daily active skincare, injectables, and advanced resurfacing procedures.

  • Board-certified Family Nurse Practitioner (NP-C)
  • Dermatology Certified Nurse Practitioner (DCNP)
  • BA, Boston University · MSN, MGH Institute of Health Professions
  • Creator of the Skin Fitness skin-conditioning framework
Meet our esthetician

Marina Kitzis, Medical Esthetician.

Over thirty years in esthetics — facial rejuvenation and the treatment of acne, mild scarring, and pigmentary changes, for both teenagers and adults. Inside a medical dermatology practice.

Three decades of training, still adding to it

Marina trained in Moscow at the Institute of Esthetics, completing an intensive two-year program with an emphasis on nutrition and holistic methods. She has worked in the Newton area for more than twenty-five years, and has continued her education with specialty courses at the Catherine Hinds and Elizabeth Grady schools of esthetics.

Facials with a clinical backbone

Marina's focus is facial rejuvenation and the treatment of acne, mild scarring, and pigmentary changes, using glycolic peels and facials for both teenagers and adults. Facials — alone or in combination with glycolic acid peels — help maintain a healthy complexion, and can be an important part of a complete acne protocol, enhancing the effectiveness of both oral and topical acne medications.

What a facial involves

A thorough cleansing of the skin and pores, in which blackheads, whiteheads, and tiny cysts known as milia are precisely removed. Often a mask finishes the procedure — to tighten pores or rehydrate the skin.

Esthetician services

Facials · Glycolic acid peels · Teen and adult acne treatment · Extractions · Pigmentation and mild scarring · Daily skin-care regimen guidance

Our services

Medical first. Everything else follows.

A full range of dermatologic care for disorders of the skin, hair, and nails — plus cosmetic dermatology and medical esthetics.

Skin cancer screening
Medical dermatology

Skin cancer prevention

Early detection remains the best method for preventing skin cancer. Regardless of the reason for your visit, we recommend a comprehensive skin examination at your initial appointment — particularly if you've had extensive sun exposure or a family history of skin cancer. It's an opportunity for the doctor to check for suspicious moles and early skin cancers, especially in areas that are difficult to examine yourself.

  • Seborrheic keratosis
  • Shingles
  • Squamous cell carcinoma
  • Tinea versicolor
  • Warts
Cosmetic dermatology

Injectables, lasers, and clinical skincare

Clinically proven active skincare ingredients, advanced skin procedures, and injectables to maintain, rejuvenate, and enhance skin — timed to your skin's condition.

  • Neurotoxins and dermal fillers — Botox, Dysport, Restylane, Juvederm
  • A variety of laser treatments
  • VI Peels — melasma, acne, acne scarring, aging skin, stretch marks, hyperpigmentation
  • ZO skincare products and Elta MD sunscreen · Alastin

To arrange a consultation with our dermatology nurse practitioner, Rachel Cohen, contact the office. Aesthetic patients can sign up for rewards before their consultation: Allē · Aspire.

The patient experience, end to end.

What a Skin Fitness participant sees across the year — application to invitation, baseline to measured progress. The persona and dates are fictional; the workflow is the real design.

The journey — pilot member since April 2026
  • Done
    Application received. April 14 · read personally, answered in two days
  • Done
    Invitation to schedule. April 16 · pilot seat confirmed
  • Done
    Initial medical exam + baseline imaging. May 4 · Phase I begins
  • Done
    Phase I · Foundation. May–June · barrier repair, daily SPF, routine locked in
  • Now
    Phase II · Active Training. Week 9 · retinoid titrated up, tolerance holding
  • Next
    Checkpoint imaging. August 12 · compared to baseline — virtual review available
  • Ahead
    Phase III · Performance → Phase IV · Maintenance. Targeted in-office work, then hold the gains
Measured progress

Every phase is documented against your own baseline — progress that is measured, not remembered. Checkpoint imaging compares to baseline on August 12. (Licensed sample imagery for demonstration.)

Privacy

Cookie policy.

What this website stores on your device, why, and how to change it. Last updated —.

The short version

This site does not sell your data, does not run advertising trackers, and does not attempt to identify you. It stores two small preferences on your device so the site behaves the way you left it.

What is stored

Name Purpose Kept
sf-themeRemembers whether you chose light or dark mode.Until cleared
sf-consentRemembers your choice below, so you are not asked again.12 months

Both are strictly necessary in the sense that they exist only to honor a preference you set. Neither is shared with anyone.

Analytics

Analytics are off unless you turn them on. If enabled, they measure page views and general traffic patterns in aggregate. They are never used to identify individuals, and are not used for advertising.

Analytics stay off on any page where you are signing in to Patient Gateway, requesting an appointment, or submitting an application, regardless of your choice.

Leaving this site

Some links take you elsewhere: Patient Gateway (Mass General Brigham), our payment processor, and downloadable patient forms. Once you follow one of those links you are on their site, under their privacy and cookie policies, not ours.

Health information

This website is not where your medical record lives. Booking and new-patient forms are handled by our booking provider, not by this website. Clinical questions, results, and photographs belong in Patient Gateway, which is the protected channel for protected health information.

Your choices

Change your decision at any time using the buttons here. You can also clear cookies in your browser settings, which resets everything on this site. This site honors Global Privacy Control signals.

Current setting: essential only
